name: multi-company-portal
description: Multi-company login portal that hosts the FinTrack financial app per tenant, with master/staff accounts.
whatsNew: Recording a withdrawal: ticking Store withdraw, Actual paid amount or Buy currency now fills in the whole dollars of the amount for you — $150.50 becomes 150 — and the 50 cents go to Unclaimed credit, the same as any other leftover. It keeps up if you change the amount, and a figure you type yourself is left alone.

The dashboard’s Date range now follows the calendar too: until you pick your own dates it shows the last 7 days up to today, and moves forward at midnight. Dates you pick yourself stay exactly as you set them — and if you only pick the From date, the To date keeps following today.

At midnight the dashboard now moves to the new day by itself. Before, “Today” could keep showing the previous day’s totals under the new day’s date until something else changed on the page. The month lists on the Monthly view and the Off Days calendar also pick up a new month straight away.

If a save doesn’t go through — a slow connection or a busy moment on the server — the app now keeps trying by itself until it does, and tells you when everything is saved. Before, an entry could show on your own screen without ever reaching anyone else’s. If you try to close the tab while something still hasn’t saved, the browser now asks first. Saves on large companies also have more time before the server gives up.

When an account is deactivated it now stops working straight away — including on any computer where it’s already open, which goes back to the login page within two minutes (or as soon as someone looks at that tab). Before, an already-open screen kept working until it was next reloaded.

Logging out now signs out only the computer you’re on. Before, logging out also signed out every other computer using the same login — so when two people shared a login, one of them logging out could sign the other out too, part-way through their work.

If the app is slow to download your company’s data — on a VPN or a weak connection, for example — it now says “Loading your company data…” with a timer, instead of an empty page that said “No active banks”. If the download fails it tells you so, confirms your data is safe, and tries again by itself. Please don’t refresh while it’s loading: refreshing starts the download again from the beginning.

The How-to guide now explains the keyboard shortcuts. Open Help → “Recording a transaction” and it walks through the Alt+letter shortcuts for opening an entry (including the two new ones, Alt+B for Bank Block and Alt+C for Buy/Sell currency) plus Enter, Tab, the arrow keys and Esc inside the form — in English, 中文 and ភាសាខ្មែរ. The collapsed shortcut strip also used to read “Alt + first letter”, which stopped being true once Buy/Sell currency took Alt+C; it now just says “Alt + a letter”.

Bank Block and Buy/Sell currency now have keyboard shortcuts of their own: on the Transactions page press Alt+B for Bank Block and Alt+C for Buy/Sell currency, the same way Alt+D already opens a Regular Deposit. They were the only two entry types without one, so the shortcut strip used to show a bare "Alt+" beside them. Every shortcut you already use is unchanged.

"Buy/Sell AUD" is now called "Buy/Sell currency", and the "Buy AUD" tick-box on a withdrawal is now "Buy currency" — on the dashboard card, the new-entry buttons, the transaction log, the Search entry-type filter, the CSV/Excel/PDF exports and the How-to guide in all three languages. The app has never tracked which currency a company keeps its books in, so the label no longer claims one. Only the wording changed: every entry already saved is untouched and still counts exactly as before.

The How-to guide now uses your own country’s banking words. Open Help and the Bank accounts, Blacklist Member and Details sections name the same boxes you actually see on screen — a Singapore company reads Bank/branch code and PayNow, India reads IFSC code and UPI ID, and so on, in English, 中文 and ភាសាខ្មែរ alike. Australian companies see the guide exactly as before.

The Bank name list and the banking wording now cover the Asia-Pacific countries, not just Australia and Singapore. A company in Cambodia, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, Indonesia, Hong Kong, China, Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, India, Malaysia or New Zealand gets its own banks in the dropdown and its own wording — for example Thailand shows PromptPay ID, India shows IFSC code and UPI ID, Malaysia shows DuitNow ID, and Hong Kong shows FPS ID. Any other country now shows “Bank/branch code” and “Payment ID” instead of the Australian terms, with Payment Gateway and Others in the bank list. Australian companies see no change at all. If your bank isn’t listed, pick Others and rename the card from the Bank Accounts page.
For Singapore companies, the example under VPN when you add a bank account now says “e.g. Singapore node” instead of Melbourne. Everyone else sees it exactly as before.

Singapore companies now see Singapore banking terms. Wherever the app used to say BSB it now says Bank/branch code, and PayID now says PayNow — on the Bank Accounts and Bank Details pages (the add and edit forms, the cards, the popup and the search boxes) and on the Blacklist Member page. The example hints change too, e.g. 7171-001 for a DBS branch, and a mobile number or UEN for PayNow. Only the wording changes: what you've saved stays exactly as it is. Companies in Australia and every other country see no change at all.

The Bank name dropdown — when you add a bank account or a bank detail — now lists the banks for your own company's country. Singapore companies see DBS, POSB, OCBC, UOB and the other Singapore banks instead of Australian ones, and Malaysia and New Zealand have their own lists too. Australian companies see exactly the same list as before. If your bank isn't listed, pick Others, then rename the card from the Bank Accounts page.

Filtering the Search page by a member now brings up all of that member's transactions. If a transaction had been recorded with the name typed a little differently — different capitals, or an extra space — picking that member from the Member dropdown did not show it, even though the same transaction did appear on the member's own page. Both screens now agree. This only ever adds rows to your results; nothing that showed before has gone.

Some members' transaction count and Total deposits on the Members page were lower than they should have been. If a transaction had been recorded with the member's name typed a little differently — different capitals, or an extra space in the middle — it was not being counted towards that member. 46 transactions across two companies were affected, worth $2,928 in deposits, and they now appear where they belong. Your company totals on the Search page were never affected by this; only the per-member figures on the Members page, the member popup and the members download. The Members page also opens and sorts noticeably faster than before.

The Members page search now finds names and phone numbers the same forgiving way the entry form and the Search page already do. Pasting a name that came through with a stray character stuck to it — "GMONIQUE FEDERICO WILLIS" instead of "Monique Federico Willis" — used to find nobody at all; now the real member comes up. It also copes with a missing middle name, first and last swapped around, a hyphen or an extra space. Phone numbers work whichever way you type them: 0412 345 678, 0412345678, +61 412 345 678 and 61412345678 all find the same person, so you no longer have to know the number was saved starting with 61. Searching by Member ID works exactly as before, and nothing you could find previously has stopped being findable — the change only ever adds results.

The Search page's Keyword box now finds names the same forgiving way the entry form does. Pasting "GMONIQUE FEDERICO WILLIS" into Keyword used to return nothing even though "Monique Federico Willis" had plenty of history; now it brings that history up, and it copes with a missing middle name, first and last swapped, hyphens and extra spaces too. Nothing you could find before has stopped being findable — the change only ever adds results. Searching by ID, bank, notes or an exact amount works exactly as it did.

Searching for a member by phone number now ignores how the number is written. Almost every number on file is stored in the international form (61…), so typing it the ordinary way — 0412 345 678 — used to find nobody at all, and you had to know to type 61 first. Now 0412 345 678, 0412345678, +61 412 345 678 and 61412345678 all find the same person, and spaces, dashes or brackets no longer matter. Typing just the first few digits, or a run from the middle, still works as before.

Searching for a member by name is far more forgiving. Pasting a name that came through with a stray character stuck to it — "GMONIQUE FEDERICO WILLIS" instead of "Monique Federico Willis" — used to find nothing at all, so the entry got filed under a brand new name and the member ended up with two records. Now the real member comes up. It also copes with a missing middle name, first and last swapped around, a hyphen, an extra space, or a full stop on the end. Anything that isn't an exact match on what you typed is labelled "similar" so you can see at a glance which row is the straight match, and the closest match is always listed first.

The popup that opens when you click a bank card now leads with the account HOLDER's name instead of the bank name, matching the card itself — several accounts often share one bank. The bank name moves to the line just below it, so nothing is lost. That line is also bigger now, and the BSB, account number and PayID are set in a clearer figure typeface so they are easier to check against a statement. The member popup's detail line got the same size increase.

The How-to guide now covers the Blacklist Member page: that the list is shared with every company in your country, that anyone can add to it, that an entry can never be edited afterwards and only a master can remove one, and that the red warning under a transaction's name or phone is a warning only — it never stops you saving.

The guide also caught up on the rest of the recent changes: sorting the Members list, the Login PIN and VPN now kept with a bank account, the online / last-seen / address line on the console team list, and the fact that managers can set the company logo too.

One correction worth knowing: the guide now says plainly that the CSV, Excel and PDF buttons on Search are for master and manager only — staff accounts don't see them. English, 中文 (Chinese) and ភាសាខ្មែរ (Khmer), as always.

The Company logo card in the console — upload, replace and remove — is now open to managers as well as masters. It works exactly the same either way, and it still only ever changes your own company's logo. The company timezone stays with masters, since changing it moves which day past entries are counted in.

Deleting a bank account now erases its Login PIN and VPN along with it. Until now a deleted bank kept both values stored quietly in the background — out of sight on screen, but still there. The confirmation message tells you this before you delete, and deleting a bank still doesn't touch any other account's details.

Bank accounts now carry a Login PIN and a VPN of their own. Add them when you create a bank account, or use Edit on any existing card. The PIN sits behind a SHOW button so it isn't left in the open on a card that stays on screen all day, and copying a record over from Bank Details brings both fields with it.

Editing a member no longer leaves a duplicate behind. Changing someone's Member ID used to add a second entry under the new ID while the old one stayed in the list — two rows for the same person, both showing the same transactions. Deleting a member sticks now as well, instead of the entry reappearing a moment later.

Three members who had already been split into two entries this way have been put back together, keeping every transaction. The Member ID and name you type when editing are also trimmed now, so a stray space at the end can't quietly create a separate record.

Every dropdown in the app now jumps as you type. Open one, start typing, and a few letters is usually enough to land on what you want instead of scrolling — press the same letter again to step through the entries that start with it.

The same bank account or PayID can no longer be added to the Blacklist Member list twice. If you type one that's already there, the form tells you straight away who it's listed under and won't let it be saved again.

Phone numbers work differently on purpose: if a number is already on the list you'll see a note saying who it belongs to, but you can still save. One person is often reported under several different names on the same number, and those are all worth recording.

The Blacklist Member page is easier to read: everything about a person now fits on screen without dragging left and right, and the list is paged like the Members directory — 50 at a time by default, or pick 100, 200, 500 or 1000.

New Blacklist Member page in the sidebar, starting with 3,441 imported records. Unlike every other page, this list is SHARED — every company in the same country sees the same entries, so anything you report shows up for them and theirs shows up for you. Anyone can add. Entries can never be edited, and only a master can remove one.

When you record a transaction, the name and phone fields now warn you if that person is on the blacklist — showing what they were reported for and by whom. It's only a warning: it never blocks you from saving the entry.

The console team list now shows who's signed in right now — a green "Online" dot with the address they're connected from, or "Last seen 20 minutes ago" plus the address they last signed in from for anyone who isn't. Only master and manager accounts can see this.
Staff accounts no longer have the CSV, Excel and PDF download buttons. Owners, masters and managers still export as before.

On the Members page, the "Newest joined" and "Oldest joined" sort options now follow each member's Joined date. Pick "Oldest joined" to put your longest-standing members at the top, or "Newest joined" for the most recent sign-ups first. (Members who joined on the same day keep the order they were entered in.)
On the Search page, the guide explains what each of the six filters does, and that typing a number in the keyword box matches an amount exactly rather than partly.
